key_insight: Small-radius, high-electronegativity A-site dopants such as Ca can simultaneously boost proton transport and chemical stability in BaCeO3-based perovskite electrolytes by weakening A–O bonding and shrinking the lattice.
engineering_relevance: A-site doping offers a practical materials-design route to improve proton-conducting solid oxide fuel cell electrolytes without relying only on B-site substitution.
method: Mechanistic analysis of A-site electronegativity and ionic-radius effects
Assessment of proton uptake, vacancy formation, impurity-phase tendency, and gas adsorption
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computed evidence that Ca doping enhances proton uptake, improves stability against CO2/SO2, and can reduce grain-boundary resistance via surface segregation.
watch_item: Benefits may depend on maintaining the right dopant level and microstructure, since excessive segregation or unintended phase formation could offset conductivity gains.
paper_title: Role of small-radius and high-electronegativity A-Site dopants in enhancing proton transport and stability of perovskite electrolytes
